correctionNotes: Sub-bass rolls off ~3-6 dB under Harman 2018 below 60 Hz (typical open-back dynamic): fill with a low shelf ~70 Hz.
Mild +2 dB warmth hump 150-250 Hz: small bell cut keeps low-mids clean when adding sub-bass boost.
Presence dip of ~2.5 dB at 4.2-4.6 kHz and ~3.5 dB at 7-7.5 kHz: gentle fills restore detail/dialogue clarity; do not over-boost the natural +1.8 dB 6 kHz energy nearby.
Deep 9.5-10 kHz notch and 12 kHz peak in the measurement are known clone-711 coupler artifacts (per Kuulokenurkka) - do NOT chase them with big boosts/cuts.

Treble above ~15 kHz rolls off sharply; headphone can sound slightly dark vs airier rivals. A small +1 dB air shelf at 11-12 kHz is enough; treble is otherwise calm and non-fatiguing, no harsh peaks need cutting.
signature: Open-back dynamic with TPCD (thin-ply carbon) diaphragm; HD600-successor neutral tuning that tracks Harman 2018 closely through mids and ear-gain, with slightly rolled sub-bass below 60 Hz, mild 150-300 Hz warmth, and calm treble that rolls off above 15 kHz.
source: Kuulokenurkka.com HEDDphone D1 review (2026-02-25) + frequency response measurement (clone IEC-60318-4 coupler, KB501X pinnae, Harman 2018 reference): https://kuulokenurkka.com/en/review-heddphone-d1/ + https://kuulokenurkka.squig.link/?share=Harman_2018_Target,HEDDphone_D1_** — AutoEq has NO D1 entry (its 'HEDD HEDDphone' entries are the older AMT models, not applicable).
